answer: Each agent holds a jade‑signed credential issued by a trusted forge that records its computational history in a shale‑based ledger. When a task is posted, the system randomly requests a proof‑of‑work signature that only the original credential can generate; forged identities lack the unique jade key and must expend full work for each fake node. The attacker therefore pays a linear cost equal to the total work of all submitted fake identities, quickly outweighing any benefit.
